steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The adult human skeleton is made up of 206 bones . At birth, humans have around 270 bones, but many fuse together as the body grows.

steps.title: Exam Tip
steps.body: The pectoral girdle (shoulder) and pelvic girdle (hip) are part of the appendicular skeleton, not the axial. A common mistake is thinking the pelvis belongs to the axial skeleton because it's in the centre of the body.

steps.title: You must know all five functions
steps.body: Support, Protection, Movement, Mineral Storage, Blood Cell Production.

steps.title: The vertebral column
steps.body: consists of 33 vertebrae stacked on top of each other, separated by intervertebral discs that act as shock absorbers.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Name the five functions of the skeleton. | How many bones make up the axial skeleton? | Give one example each of a long bone, a short bone, a flat bone and an irregular bone.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Support, protection, movement, mineral storage, blood cell production. | 80 bones make up the axial skeleton. | Long: femur; Short: carpals; Flat: cranium; Irregular: vertebrae.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always use the correct scientific names for bones (e.g. femur, not "thigh bone") Link bone classification to function - examiners want to see you understand WHY a bone is shaped that way The mnemonic "Breakfast at 7, Lunch at 12, Dinner at 5" helps remember cervical/thoracic/lumbar vertebrae counts When asked about functions, state all five - don't just list two or three Know the difference between axial (80) and appendicular (126) skeleton bone counts Be ready to explain how bone shape relates to function in sporting contexts
